sense: ill-treat a person or an animal

terms.comment: Properly to shake or toss about (Gellius explains it as stronger than vehere, 2.6.5); then the general word for harassing and ill-treating people, lands and things.

terms.grammar: phrase: injūriōsē with tractō, tractāre, tractāvī, tractātum
evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 11: mercātōrēs ac nāviculāriī injūriōsius tractātī (Lewis & Short, s.v. tractō)
terms.comment: Also injūriā afficere, to do someone wrong. Tractāre alone means to treat or handle, well or badly.

phrases.latin: In calamitōsō rīsus etiam injūria est.
phrases.english: laughing at someone in trouble is itself a wrong
Leave the cat alone, don’t torment it.

sources: Lewis & Short: vexo · Lewis & Short: tracto · Lewis & Short: injuria
